journey.title: Focus stays in the results dialog after Show all removes itself
journey.goal: Activating a control that removes itself keeps keyboard focus inside the trapped dialog

functionalJourney.title: Show all results with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: The dialog opens, lists every result and closes

guards.title: Escape closes results and returns focus
guards.goal: Escape dismisses the dialog and focus returns to the trigger

plan.root_cause: The focus trap's checkKeyNav function lacks a fallback destination node when no tabbable groups are found, allowing browser-default focus movement to escape the trap. In the observed case, focus escaped to the body element when tabbing from the last tabbable node.
plan.repair_strategy: Enhance the else branch in checkKeyNav to provide a destination node by attempting to focus the first focusable node in the first container, or the container itself as a last resort, when fallbackFocus is not set.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus will remain confined within the dialog when tabbing from the last focusable element, preventing accidental focus loss for keyboard users.
functional_risks: Focusing the container (a non-focusable div) is harmless but unconventional; however, it is preferable to losing focus entirely.
If the first focusable node in the container has tabindex=-1, it may receive focus unexpectedly, but this is a rare fallback scenario.
verification_requirements: Pressing Tab from the close button should move focus to the more button, and pressing Tab again should move focus back to the close button (not escape to the body).
Repeated Tab presses should cycle focus between the close and more buttons without escaping the dialog.
Pressing Escape should close the dialog and return focus to the trigger button.

plan.root_cause: The focus trap's `checkFocusIn` function does not validate that the `mostRecentlyFocusedNode` is still in the document and contained within the trap before attempting to refocus it. When the focused element is removed from the DOM (e.g., the "Show all" button removes itself), the focus escapes to the body, and the fallback node is the removed element, which cannot receive focus, causing focus to remain on the body.
plan.repair_strategy: Enhance `checkFocusIn` to verify the fallback node is still in the document and within a trap container; if not, use `getInitialFocusNode()` to find a valid focus target.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus remains trapped within the dialog when the currently focused element is removed, preventing focus loss for keyboard users.
functional_risks: Minimal; the fallback logic only activates when focus escapes, and the additional checks are safe.
If the document contains check fails for shadow DOM nodes, the fallback will still trigger getInitialFocusNode which is correct.
verification_requirements: Pressing Enter on the "more" button should keep focus within the dialog (on the close button or first tabbable element).
Repeated Tab presses should cycle focus between the close button and other tabbable elements without escaping the dialog.
Pressing Escape should close the dialog and return focus to the trigger button.

plan.root_cause: The focus trap's `checkFocusIn` function does not update its internal tabbable node groups before attempting to restore focus after an escape. When the focused element (the "Show all" button) is removed from the DOM by the application, the trap's `state.tabbableGroups` still references the removed button. Consequently, `getInitialFocusNode()` returns a stale reference to the removed button, which cannot receive focus, causing focus to remain on the body element.
plan.repair_strategy: Update the tabbable node groups inside `checkFocusIn` when focus has escaped the trap, ensuring that `getInitialFocusNode()` returns a current, valid focus target (the close button) instead of a removed element.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus remains trapped within the dialog when the currently focused element is removed from the DOM, preventing focus loss for keyboard users.
functional_risks: Minimal; the additional `updateTabbableNodes()` call only occurs when focus has already escaped, and the function is already used during keyboard navigation.
If the dialog somehow loses all tabbable nodes, `updateTabbableNodes()` will throw an error, but the trap requires at least one tabbable node at all times.
verification_requirements: Pressing Enter on the "Show all" button should keep focus within the dialog (on the close button or first tabbable element).
Repeated Tab presses should cycle focus between the close button and other tabbable elements without escaping the dialog.
Pressing Escape should close the dialog and return focus to the trigger button.
